name: Willow
description: A single-file H5 medicine tracker whose world model is subtraction with consequences. Each medicine has a number of tablets left and a schedule, and those two produce a third figure — how many days before it runs out — which is never stored, only divided. Marking a dose taken removes a tablet and brings that date closer; skipping leaves the count alone and dents the adherence figure instead; ordering a repeat adds a whole pack; adding a second dose time halves the days remaining. Six medicines are seeded at deliberately different depths, so 'which runs out first' has to be worked out. 6 screens, 3 dose times, a repeat-ordering flow and a week of history.

finish.answer: final answer for question tasks; optional for action tasks

observation.text: engine.a11y(state) — every dose row, the tablets left and the days remaining serialise, and the take/skip buttons appear only when they are actually on screen.
observation.pixels: 390x844 screenshot (browser backend); __ENV__.bounds() maps every test-id to a pixel box
observation.state: engine.snapshot(state) — canonical state plus a derived view keyed by medicine name. For the verifier only.

world.today: Tuesday, 08:15 — the morning doses are due
world.days_left: tablets left divided by the daily dose, rounded down
world.taken_vs_skipped: taking removes a tablet, skipping does not; both close the dose for the day
world.repeats: a medicine is 'low' at or under the warning threshold in Settings, and a repeat adds one whole pack
world.caution: one seeded interaction: leave four hours between Levothyroxine and Vitamin D
